string.text: Callback monitoring, performance profiling, and testing.
Log top-firing callbacks at regular intervals.
[seconds]\nHow often to log periodic statistics. Range 10-3600.
Log callback arguments/parameters. Can create large log files.
Extract detailed info from objects (type, name, section, community).
Maximum depth for table introspection (1-4). Higher = more detail but larger logs.
Scan smart terrain distances, stash density, base spacing, and feature distribution per level. Fires on level load and periodically. Log output: logs/testzone.log

For when every timer in the game stops at once: HUDs never appear, stat panels freeze, and nothing is logged. Records whether the timer queue registered at load and which timer broke it. After a freeze, run_string tz_watcher.log_queue_state() names the timer left mid-call. Takes effect on the next game load. Log output: logs/testzone.log
Limit log frequency per callback type. Prevents log spam from high-frequency callbacks.
[milliseconds]\nMinimum time between logs for same callback type. Range 100-10000.
Opens the AnimationTool on the stalker you look at. Esc closes it.
Periodic scan of all mutant squads. Logs species, faction, online/offline, smart terrain, commander fields.
[seconds]\nHow often the mutant scan runs. Range 5-300.
Periodic scan of the current level: squads, smart terrains, stashes, and the AP squad overlay.
[seconds]\nHow often the level scan runs. Range 10-300.
World-wide squad census: totals by faction, by level, and online/offline counts.
[seconds]\nHow often the world scan runs. Range 30-600.
Watcher logs all 162 engine callbacks. Log output: logs/testzone.log
Wraps suspect GAMMA mod functions with timing to measure actual frame cost.
Start recording timing data for wrapped functions. Functions are always wrapped, this controls measurement.
[seconds]\nHow often to log profiler report. Range 10-300.
[microseconds]\nSingle call exceeding this value counts as a spike. Range 100-10000.
Profiler wraps 22 suspect functions identified from GAMMA review. Log output: logs/testzone.log
What the stalkers and mutants near you hear, see, remember, take as danger and pick as enemy. One line per change. Output: logs/testzone_perception.log
Every hearing event that reaches him, with its power against his threshold. One line per source and sound type per half second.
When he starts or stops seeing you, and his detection progress in 10 percent steps.
His visual, sound and hit memory of you: presence, age and payload, on every change. Mutants: visual only.
His held danger with the action answering it down to the leaf (take cover, look out, hold, detour, search), and his reaction with the distance he moved. Stalkers only.
Who he picks as enemy and drops, and whether this log saw him hear or see you before the pick.
Subjects within this distance of you are tracked (meters).
Hearing events from every source, not only yours. One line per subject and source per second at most.
Track mutants as well as stalkers. Every line carries the kind.
Reads engine state only. Works the same with any AI mod on or off, so two runs compare. Log output: logs/testzone_perception.log
GeoTool shows every place check live at your spot and saves notes with the position and the readings to logs/geo_tool.txt.
Opens the GeoTool window. Esc closes it.
[seconds] How often the open window reads every check.
Notes go to logs/geo_tool.txt, one tab-separated line each.
SoundTool plays DiegeticAmbience channels, DiegeticDread categories, NPC voice and any .ogg on disk, and writes your tags and notes to logs/sound_tool.txt.
Opens the SoundTool window. Esc closes it.
Logs every sound the soundscape plays, with its channel, distance, map and weather, to logs/testzone_sound_trace.log.
The sound trace also logs script sounds outside the ambient channels, such as music, the interface and DiegeticDread's cues.
Files from outside the game are copied into sounds/sound_tool_cache while the window is open and deleted when it closes.
Logging level and flush for every TestZone subsystem. Output: logs/testzone.log
Minimum severity written to the log. DEBUG shows everything, ERROR almost nothing.
Write each line to disk at once instead of buffering. Slower, but the log stays current while you tail it.
Restore all TestZone MCM settings to defaults. Use after upgrading from a version with a different MCM structure.
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first, otherwise they override the reset on the next Apply.
TestZone: all settings restored to defaults.

GeoTool shows what every place check says at your spot, live while the window is open. When a check reads your spot wrong, you write so in a note, and the note keeps the spot and every reading.
 
The top screen shows the level, the level vertex and your position as X, Y and Z in whole metres.
 
The middle screen holds the readings, and the green lamp stays lit while they refresh. Smart is the nearest smart terrain, its distance, and whether it is a base or a lair. Base owner is the nearest trader, medic or mechanic within 80 metres. Is indoor is the xlibs test, a roof within 4 metres and two walls within 5. Roof is the roof alone, from a ray up or, when that misses, a ray down. Roof walls is the raw roof distance and wall count behind the xlibs test. Underground says whether the level counts as underground. Surge cover says whether the emission treats your spot as cover, and safe cover whether the game flags you as sheltered. Rain is how much rain reaches you. Sky is how much open sky lights you, and below 0.05 the game counts you as indoor.
 
Type a note and press the plus key, and it goes to logs/geo_tool.txt as a tab-separated line. That line holds the time, the level, your position, the level vertex and every reading, and an empty note saves the spot with its readings alone. Your last two notes show on the bottom screen.
 
Del opens the window and Esc closes it, and MCM can change the open key and how often the readings refresh.

AnimationTool plays a motion or a state on a stalker, and you judge it good or bad in the anim curation file in the logs folder.
 
Look at a stalker and press the open key, PgDn unless MCM changed it. The tool binds him for as long as the window stays open. The screen shows his name, then the state last asked of him and, after the arrow, the animation he plays now, refreshed twice a second. Select pins the stalker you aim at, or the bound one when you aim at no one, and keeps him bound every time you reopen the tool. Its diode stays lit until Reset drops him.
 
The list shows every .tsv or .txt file in configs/testzone/anim. Click a file, then click a motion to select it. Play or a double click plays it on the stalker, Stop sends him back to idle, and Prev and Next step to the neighbouring motion and play it. The green lamp stays lit while a motion holds on him, and the red lamp lights when it stops.
 
Pose plays a motion standing in place, and moving plays it while he walks. A click on either key replays the motion at once. A state from the dig list plays the way the game wires it and ignores both keys.
 
The prop row at the top of a list attaches an item, a bottle, a guitar or a knife, from the next play on, until you pick none again.
 
Good and bad log the selected motion with your typed note, the plus key logs the typed note alone, and the bottom screen shows the last two entries.
 
A motion plays only when that stalker has its animation file loaded, and an unknown name plays nothing. Esc closes the tool and returns the stalker to idle.

SoundTool plays a sound the way the game plays it, or at a distance you pick, and you tag what you hear in logs/sound_tool.txt.
 
The list starts with browse files, then each DiegeticDread category and each DiegeticAmbience channel when that mod is installed. Browse files opens the logs folder. Two dots go up a folder, and above a drive the list shows every drive. Play this folder lists the folder's .ogg files, and a .txt file opens as a playlist. The loop key at the top reads the categories and channels again.
 
A playlist line is a game path like zs/spook/raven_1, an absolute path, or a path next to the playlist. A comment line with base: and a folder makes the next relative lines start there, and a line that names no file and no folder is a divider.
 
The game plays only the files it has indexed, and a file from outside the game is copied into sounds/sound_tool_cache first. A rescan follows each batch of copies and can take half a second. The cache empties when the window opens and when it closes.
 
A click on a sound plays it. Prev and next move without playing, and Stop ends only the sounds this tool started. The green lamp stays lit while one of them still plays, and the red lamp lights when the last one ends.
 
The three mode keys set where the sound plays. As heard plays it where the game would, near, felt or far for an ambience channel and at a dread level for a dread sound. 2D plays it at your ear, and 3D plays it in front of you from 5 to 100 metres. A click on the lit mode key steps to its next distance or dread level. The volume keys set how loud the next play is, from 0.1 to 1.0. As heard is off for a voice line or a plain file, because the game places neither of them.
 
The screen shows where the sound belongs, where it plays and how loud it arrives, and the line under the tags names the sound your tags go to. A tag writes the sound's path, family, mode and tag, with your typed note after it, and the plus key writes the typed note alone. The bottom screen shows the last two lines written. The DiegeticDread director stays silent while the window is open, and its replay of the base ambience too.
 
End opens the window and Esc closes it, and MCM can change the open key.
